html:
The Nogai Horde was a confederation of Turkic speaking Muslim nomads on the steppe north of the Caspian and Black Seas, from the 1400s to the 1600s. It was one of the pieces left when the Golden Horde fell apart.

Its core was the Manghit tribe. Its founder is usually taken to be Edigu, a Manghit general who was the real power in the Golden Horde around 1400. Unlike the khans, Nogai leaders did not descend from Genghis Khan, so they ruled as begs or mirzas, often as kingmakers for the Kazan, Astrakhan and Crimean khanates.

The Nogais lived by herding horses and sheep and sold huge herds of horses to Muscovy every year. After Muscovy took Kazan and Astrakhan in the 1550s, the horde split into a Great Horde on the Volga and a Lesser Horde in the North Caucasus. In the early 1600s the Kalmyks, Mongol nomads from the east, drove the Nogais west. Nogai people still live in the North Caucasus.
